findings.title: Shared @cipherstash/stack native client with an AsyncLocalStorage getJwt still binds users to the wrong identity
findings.label: valid
findings.note: The skill's headline says a module-level strategy is fine while the stack native path calls getJwt from a Neon channel outside the caller's ALS context, so a shared client can bind users to the wrong identity, and no test covers it.

findings.title: Go strategy shared across users serialises every user's provider call and CTS exchange behind one mutex
findings.label: valid
findings.note: Strategy.Token holds the mutex for the whole guest call, and the provider and per-user exchanges now run inside it, so one slow user's IdP call or CTS round trip blocks every user on a shared Go strategy.

findings.title: More CTS exchanges from JWT rotation and legacy stored tokens; an account refusal then blocks every new user
findings.label: valid
findings.note: BoundStore treats unstamped tokens as a miss and the cache is keyed per JWT, so exchange volume rises; a strategy-wide account-refusal denial then blocks every uncached JWT for the TTL, as the cited code shows.

findings.title: Guidance to share clients outlives the fix: version skew or rollback reintroduces #1045
findings.label: trivial
findings.note: The skill already tells users of releases before the #1045 fix to build one client per user; a missing version number is a minor docs gap, and the rollback scenario is speculative.
